declaration: I give in secret, because my Father sees what is done in secret.
I pray with a steady rhythm, and I expect Him to answer.
I fast with purpose, and I keep my heart ready for what He is doing.

days.takeaway: Lasting growth comes from simple disciplines practised day after day, not from hype or quick promises.
days.reflect: What would you like God to grow in you this year, and what small step will you take first?
days.doToday: Write down one thing you are asking God to grow in you and pray over it once.

days.takeaway: Giving, praying and fasting are three habits Jesus expected His followers to practise, and together they shape a changed life.
days.reflect: Which of the three do you find easiest, and which would stretch you most?
days.doToday: Pick one of the three to practise today, however small.

days.takeaway: Giving is an act of the heart: trust, love and generosity that go beyond money alone.
days.reflect: What can you give today that costs time, attention or kindness rather than money?
days.doToday: Give someone your full attention for five minutes, with your phone put away.

days.takeaway: Prayer costs time and effort, and time given to God is never wasted; it deepens trust in Him.
days.reflect: What does the time you spend with God show about what you value most right now?
days.doToday: Set aside ten quiet minutes before the day gets busy and pray in them.

days.takeaway: Fasting is more than going without food; it prepares body, mind and spirit to hear God clearly.
days.reflect: What might God be preparing you for that needs a clearer heart and mind?
days.doToday: Plan one meal to be simpler today and use that pause to pray.

days.takeaway: When giving, praying and fasting work together, each one strengthens the others and the whole life grows.
days.reflect: How could one of these support another in your week, for example prayer shaping how you give?
days.doToday: Link one act of giving with one prayer and one simpler meal today.

days.takeaway: Joy in fasting comes from knowing its purpose and keeping your heart turned toward God.
days.reflect: What would make this fast feel like a gift to you rather than a burden?
days.doToday: Thank God for three things before you begin your fast or meal today.

days.takeaway: Jesus said to anoint your head when you fast, so that your fast shows a glad heart and not a gloomy face.
days.reflect: What would it look like to fast with a glad heart instead of a heavy one?
days.doToday: Wash your face, begin with a short prayer of thanks, and let your fast be quiet and glad.

days.takeaway: Faith is spoken as well as held; declaring God's promises out loud gives your faith words and direction.
days.reflect: Which promise of God will you speak out loud this week, and where will you say it?
days.doToday: Say one promise of God out loud twice, then write it on a card.

days.takeaway: Matthew 6 teaches that fasting is between you and your Father, done quietly rather than for applause.
days.reflect: How would your fast change if no one at home or school ever knew about it?
days.doToday: Fast or simplify one meal today without mentioning it to anyone.

days.takeaway: Jesus taught prayer that begins with relationship: calling God Father, near and holy in heaven.
days.reflect: What does calling God 'Our Father' change about how you come to Him?
days.doToday: Begin today's prayer with 'Our Father in heaven' and then speak in your own words.

days.takeaway: Prayer grows strong when it lines up with God's will, asking for what He has already said He cares about.
days.reflect: What does God's Word say about the request on your heart right now?
days.doToday: Find one Bible promise that matches your prayer request and read it aloud.

days.takeaway: Many prayers stall when something essential is missing, and honest reflection helps you find what needs to change.
days.reflect: What might be missing from your prayers that you have never named before?
days.doToday: Ask God to show you one thing that may be hindering your prayers, then listen quietly.

days.takeaway: The attitude you pray in, humble, sincere and trusting, matters as much as the words you use.
days.reflect: What attitude do you bring when you pray, and what attitude would you like to bring?
days.doToday: Before you pray, take a breath and ask God for a humble, trusting heart.

days.takeaway: Some truths about giving, praying and fasting are learned only by practising them and seeing God at work.
days.reflect: What have you noticed about God during a season of practising these disciplines?
days.doToday: Write one thing you have learned from prayer, giving or fasting this week.

days.takeaway: A threefold cord is hard to break, and giving, praying and fasting done in secret hold a life steady together.
days.reflect: Which of the three cords is weakest in your life right now?
days.doToday: Do one act of secret kindness or giving today and tell no one.

days.takeaway: Joy makes giving, praying and fasting lighter, and a glad, thankful heart is a good place to meet God.
days.reflect: What brings you joy that you could bring into your prayer time?
days.doToday: Spend five minutes thanking and praising God before you pray.

days.takeaway: Giving, praying and fasting strengthen one another when practised together, but faithfulness matters more than any formula.
days.reflect: What would faithful, steady practice look like for you over the next few weeks?
days.doToday: Choose one time this week to repeat a discipline you have already started.

days.takeaway: The call is to live giving, praying and fasting on purpose, centred on Christ and not on self.
days.reflect: What would intentional living around Christ look like in your home or school this week?
days.doToday: Name the purpose of your next fast in one sentence before you begin.
